name: Polypodium leucotomos

lead: Polypodium leucotomos is a tropical fern native to Central and South America whose leaf extract is sold as an oral supplement, for example under the Fernblock and Heliocare names. It has a long history in traditional medicine and has been studied in dermatology for UV-related skin reactions.

In the appearance space it is used as an "internal sunscreen" adjunct to reduce sunburn, photoaging and pigmentation. Clinical studies suggest modest benefit, but it is not a substitute for sunscreen.

paras: The extract is rich in phenolic compounds with antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activity. In studies it reduces UV-induced DNA damage and inflammatory mediators, limits generation of reactive oxygen species, and may support Langerhans cell function in skin. It does not absorb UV like a sunscreen filter.

Oral extract is generally well tolerated, with occasional mild gastrointestinal upset, headache or itching; serious adverse effects have not been reported in published reviews. Evidence comes from small trials with varied formulations, so supplements that do not specify the studied extract may not be equivalent.
